llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (create/manage ERC-4337 accounts) matches the actions described in SKILL.md, but the registry-level required environment variables and metadata are broader and less conditional than the runtime instructions require—this mismatch could result in over-privileged secret exposure unless clarified.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to create, fund, and manage ERC-4337 smart accounts and the instructions describe RPC interaction, contract calls, and use of an external signer—these are coherent with the stated purpose. However, the registry metadata lists signer endpoint/auth token and dashboard API key as always required, while SKILL.md says some of these are only needed for specific signing modes (e.g., external_signer) or only for dashboard interactions. That unconditional requirement appears disproportionate to the declared capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within the expected scope: it prepares transactions, reads chain state via a public client, and forwards transactions to an external signer or prompts user wallet depending on signing_mode. It explicitly forbids asking for private keys in chat and cautions about storing secrets. There are no instructions to read local files or unrelated environment variables. The only scope note is that forwarding transactions to a signer endpoint (and requiring an auth token) enables the skill to initiate signed on-chain actions; this is intended but powerful and should be limited by signer-side policy.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, so nothing is written to disk by an installer. That minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest requires six environment variables (GUARDRAIL_CHAIN_ID, GUARDRAIL_RPC_URL, GUARDRAIL_SIGNING_MODE, GUARDRAIL_SIGNER_ENDPOINT, GUARDRAIL_SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN, GUARDRAIL_DASHBOARD_API_KEY). SKILL.md documents that some (SIGNER_ENDPOINT, SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN, DASHBOARD_API_KEY) are only necessary for particular modes or for dashboard interactions. Requiring them unconditionally is disproportionate: a user who wants read-only or wallet_connector flows should not have to provide a signing auth token. GUARDRAIL_SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN is a sensitive credential that grants signing capability when combined with the endpoint; listing it as always required increases risk of credential exposure or misuse. PrimaryEnv set to GUARDRAIL_RPC_URL is reasonable.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there is no install-time persistence, so the skill does not request elevated platform privileges. However, because the skill can be invoked autonomously (platform default) and is capable of preparing transactions and calling an external signer with an auth token, granting it secrets and enabling autonomous invocation would allow it to submit on-chain transactions without further human approval. That is expected for this use case but worth guarding with signer-side allowlists, rate limits, and/or agent-level human approval policies.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling this skill, verify these items: 1) Only provide the signer endpoint/auth token if you intend to use the external_signer mode — do not store or supply long-lived owner private keys. 2) Prefer wallet_connector or short-lived session_key modes where possible so the skill cannot sign transactions autonomously. 3) If you must use an external signer, ensure the signer enforces strict allowlists, rate limits, per-policy spend caps, and that the auth token scope is minimal and revokable. 4) Treat GUARDRAIL_SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN and GUARDRAIL_DASHBOARD_API_KEY as highly sensitive and keep them in a secure secret store; do not paste them into chat. 5) Ask the skill author/maintainer why the registry requires signer and dashboard credentials unconditionally; request a manifest that marks them optional or conditional on signing_mode. 6) Verify contract addresses, fee-manager and factory addresses, and request audits or review tests on a testnet before funding accounts on mainnet. 7) If you want to prevent autonomous on-chain activity, disable autonomous invocation or require human approval for any signing operations.
